Yes, there is a one in a certain chance that it was yours, but in your case it wasn't. The odds of it seeming to happen, and you seeing it, and you noticing it, and it not being a trick of the mind, and you just happening to fail to confirm that it's not just trick of the mind by taking a screenshot, and it actually really having happened for reals, are astronomically unlikely. Astronomically unlikely events only happen in under two circumstances, and only one applies to you. First is when you construct the probability chain after the fact, such as all the events of all your ancestors all the way back to the origin of life had to occur just as they did for you to have been born or for some particular thing to have occurred in your life. This is the only kind of astronomically unlikely events to apply to you or to any individual. The second kind is very unlikely events which are constructed ahead of time, that are very unlikely to happen to any particular person, but are not unlikely to happen to some particular person within the greater population, such as with a lottery. Now, having said that, in the history of all captchas, someone may actually experience what you thought you experienced, but possibly not. I don't have an accurate estimation of the probability of it actually occurring, but my hunch is that it won't ever happen to anyone, and that's even factoring in the probability of it intentionally occurring to anyone who doesn't have direct connection to the developers. For people with direct connections to the developers, the odds are still small, but not astronomically small. So could it technically have occurred? Yes. Sorry to disappoint, but unless you can definitively prove that it occurred, which you failed to do, the only reasonable and sane explanation is that you were mistaken. You could perhaps still rummage through your web browser's cache to try and prove it to yourself, but I assure you that it'll be a waste of your time.
